headline: 624 detained in Cumilla in drive against teen gangs
summary: Police conducted simultaneous raids across 18 police stations in the district to curb criminal activities involving teenagers.
details: Police have detained 624 people in Cumilla on suspicion of involvement in teenage gangs. The district-wide operation was carried out on Wednesday night across all 18 police station jurisdictions.
Cumilla Additional Superintendent of Police Lutfur Rahman stated that the detainees are being questioned to verify information and determine if they have previous criminal records.
The raids were targeted at locations in Cumilla city and other areas where residents had complained of harassment by groups of youths.
The operation was ordered by Superintendent of Police Md Anisuzzaman after police observed an increase in teenagers' involvement in criminal activities.
The crackdown on teen gangs has gained renewed focus following the killing of 13-year-old Ishayat Shahriar Apratim, the son of a Cumilla University teacher.
During the operation, 17 detainees reportedly escaped from a room at Daudkandi Police Station by breaking down a door due to overcrowding.
Police officials confirmed that those who escaped were later recaptured by local people and brought back to the station.
caption:
624 people detained in a single night across Cumilla. Police launch massive crackdown on 'teen gangs'.

Police have detained 624 people in Cumilla on suspicion of involvement in teenage gangs. The district-wide operation was carried out on Wednesday night across all 18 police station jurisdictions.

Cumilla Additional Superintendent of Police Lutfur Rahman stated that the detainees are being questioned to verify information and determine if they have previous criminal records.

The raids were targeted at locations in Cumilla city and other areas where residents had complained of harassment by groups of youths.

The operation was ordered by Superintendent of Police Md Anisuzzaman after police observed an increase in teenagers' involvement in criminal activities.

The crackdown on teen gangs has gained renewed focus following the killing of 13-year-old Ishayat Shahriar Apratim, the son of a Cumilla University teacher.

During the operation, 17 detainees reportedly escaped from a room at Daudkandi Police Station by breaking down a door due to overcrowding.

Police officials confirmed that those who escaped were later recaptured by local people and brought back to the station.

headline_marked: US Judge [[blocks Trump’s White House media ban]] on CNN and others
headline: US Judge blocks Trump’s White House media ban on CNN and others
summary: A federal judge ruled the ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico was likely unconstitutional, ordering the administration to restore their press passes immediately.
details: A US District Judge, Tim Kelly, has ordered President Donald Trump to restore White House access for journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, ruling that the ban was likely unconstitutional.

The judge rejected the government's claim that the ban was based on national security concerns, noting that Trump himself had attributed the ban to the 'lack of truthfulness and negativity' of the reporting.
The court ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets' press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days.
The news organizations had sued the administration, arguing that the ban violated the First Amendment's protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights.
A coalition of press freedom groups, including Reuters, the Washington Post, and Fox News, filed a legal brief supporting the three news outlets.
The Justice Department had argued that White House access is a privilege, not an entitlement, and that the president has the authority to suspend access.
The legal battle occurred just weeks before the Nov 3 midterm elections, amid record low job approval ratings for President Trump.
caption:
A US judge has ruled that Donald Trump's ban on several major news outlets was likely unconstitutional.

A US District Judge, Tim Kelly, has ordered President Donald Trump to restore White House access for journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, ruling that the ban was likely unconstitutional.

The judge rejected the government's claim that the ban was based on national security concerns, noting that Trump himself had attributed the ban to the 'lack of truthfulness and negativity' of the reporting.

The court ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets' press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days.

The news organizations had sued the administration, arguing that the ban violated the First Amendment's protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights.

A coalition of press freedom groups, including Reuters, the Washington Post, and Fox News, filed a legal brief supporting the three news outlets.

The Justice Department had argued that White House access is a privilege, not an entitlement, and that the president has the authority to suspend access.

The legal battle occurred just weeks before the Nov 3 midterm elections, amid record low job approval ratings for President Trump.
